correctness.rationale: For each fixed complex dimension d≥1, the radial Toeplitz operator is scalar on degree-n holomorphic polynomials with multiplicity binomial(n+d−1,d−1), eigenvalue E[e^{iG_k^alpha}] for G_k~Gamma(k,1), k=n+d. For 0<alpha<1/2, Gamma concentration controls phase drift O(k^{alpha−1/2}); alpha=1/2 follows delta-method normal fluctuation with damping exp(−1/8). For alpha>1/2, truncate at |G_k−k|≤k^{1/2+epsilon}, use Chernoff outside and repeated nonstationary integration by parts inside, with each derivative gaining k^{−(alpha−1/2−epsilon)}, yielding O(k^−M) for every M. Polynomial degree multiplicity gives all Schatten S_p; alpha≤1/2 is noncompact. For alpha≤1/2, Weyl phase equidistribution of k^alpha mod 2pi (alpha<1) and Abel summation for multiplicities give Haar limit and circle essential spectrum; decay yields {0} above boundary. The alpha=1 exact gamma characteristic function and gamma quadratures at k=20,50,100 separately corroborated the threshold behavior, not the infinite proof.
